memoryText: Great and amazing are your deeds, O Lord God the Almighty! Just and true are your ways, O King of the nations! Who will not fear, O Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are holy.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Revelation 15:3-4 slowly, several times, and try to say it from memory. Then read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
This is a song sung by those who have come through great trouble. Standing on the shore of the sea of glass, with harps in hand, they sing about the character of God, not about themselves.

“Great and amazing are your deeds.” They praise what he has done. “Just and true are your ways.” They praise how he does it: with justice and truth, even when the ways are painful or hard to understand. The people who sing this have seen suffering, and they still say his ways are just.

“Who will not fear, O Lord, and glorify your name? For you alone are holy.” The right response to a holy God is reverent fear and glad glory.

The song combines the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb: the exodus and the cross. When you feel confused by events, sing this to remind yourself of what will be said at the end.
weekInReview: This week you read the second half of Revelation’s visions of conflict. Chapter 14 showed the Lamb with his people on Mount Zion, the eternal gospel proclaimed to every nation, the fall of Babylon, the blessing on those who die in the Lord, and the final harvest. Chapter 15 gave us the song of Moses and the Lamb. Four psalms framed the reign of God: Psalm 2 (the nations rage, but God’s Son is enthroned), Psalm 46 (God is our refuge, be still), Psalm 93 (the LORD reigns, mightier than the floods), and Psalm 97 (the LORD reigns, light is sown for the righteous). Chapter 16 poured out the seven bowls of wrath: judgments that are just, and hearts that do not repent, ending with the cry “It is done!”
reflectionQuestions: Psalm 2 says, “Blessed are all who take refuge in him.” What would it mean for you to take refuge in Christ this week, specifically from something that frightens you?
In Revelation 16, people suffer terrible judgments and still do not repent. What does this tell you about the human heart, and how does it increase your gratitude for grace?

Revelation 14:13 says those who die in the Lord are blessed, because they rest from their labors and their deeds follow them. How does this change how you think about death, and about the work you are doing now?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that great and amazing are his deeds.
